clue.text: Form a line — ignore soldier

indicators.note: to form something is to shape it, so these letters are shaped into a new word

explanation.surface: A drill sergeant barks at the ranks to fall into line and not ignore orders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Form' is the anagram signal: the eleven letters of A LINE and IGNORE are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A legionnaire is a member of a legion, especially the French Foreign Legion, so a type of soldier.

clue.text: One is slow to pull up following delay

indicators.note: following means the word for pull comes after the word for delay

parts.note: a lag is a delay

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for pull is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to drag something is to pull it

explanation.surface: Someone sluggish has to pull themselves up after holding everyone else up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses the word for pull, giving GARD; 'to' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A laggard is a person who dawdles and falls behind the rest.

clue.text: Information about artistic style

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A gallery leaflet gives information about a painter's style.
explanation.definitionFit: A genre is a category or kind of art, music or writing.

clue.text: Eggs, not veal, oddly omitted

indicators.note: with the odd-placed letters of the words not veal dropped, the even-placed ones remain

explanation.surface: A vegetarian diner orders eggs and pointedly asks for no veal.
explanation.walkthrough: From NOTVEAL drop the first, third, fifth and seventh letters to leave the second, fourth and sixth.
explanation.definitionFit: Ova is the Latin-derived plural for egg cells, a crossword staple for eggs.

clue.text: Dub celebrity

explanation.definitionFit: To dub someone is to give them a title; a celebrity is a big public figure, a household word.

clue.text: High-risk batting — Kent's remedy?

parts.note: a batter who is batting in cricket is said to be in
Kent is a county in South East England, abbreviated SE
a cure is a remedy

explanation.surface: A cricket commentator wonders whether a nervy Kent batsman can find a remedy for his risky strokes.
explanation.walkthrough: KENT is an English county in the south-east, hence SE; in cricket a side batting is 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something insecure is unsafe or unprotected, hence exposed to danger.

clue.text: Strange sound coming from bird's nest

indicators.note: sound tells us the word for strange is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: eerie means strange and unsettling

explanation.surface: An odd noise drifts down from a bird's nest high on a cliff.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyrie is the lofty nest of an eagle or other bird of prey.

clue.text: Stopped outside right and crumpled

indicators.note: outside means the word for stopped is wrapped round the letter for right

parts.note: ceased means stopped

explanation.surface: Someone halted outside and their right side gave way in a heap.
explanation.definitionFit: A creased garment or sheet is wrinkled and folded, crumpled.

clue.text: Glass container for sailing ship

explanation.definitionFit: A schooner is a tall drinking glass for sherry or beer, and also a fore-and-aft rigged vessel with two or more masts.

clue.text: French police information leading 500 weapons, it's rumoured

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
D is the Roman numeral for 500

indicators.note: something rumoured is passed on by word of mouth, so the word for weapons is heard, not spelt

parts.note: arms are weapons

explanation.surface: French officers hear intelligence that a large haul of guns is reportedly on its way.
explanation.definitionFit: Gendarmes are the armed officers of France's national police force.

clue.text: Survey's initial result — Europe backs Europe!

indicators.note: initial picks out the first letter of the word result

parts.note: EC stands for the European Community

indicators.note: backs means the second abbreviation for Europe is turned round

parts.note: EC again, for European Community

explanation.surface: A poll result shows Europe throwing its weight behind Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backs' turns the second EC into CE.
explanation.definitionFit: A recce is military slang for a reconnaissance, a preliminary survey of ground.

clue.text: The way to a concourse?

parts.note: a concourse is a gathering, and a venue is the place where people gather

explanation.surface: Someone asks for directions to the main hall of a station.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'concourse' is being stretched to mean a meeting place.
explanation.definitionFit: An avenue is a broad road, and figuratively a route or means of approach.

clue.text: Peacekeepers fired in the dark

parts.note: UN peacekeepers belong to the United Nations
lit means set alight, fired

explanation.surface: Blue-helmeted troops come under fire at night.
explanation.definitionFit: Somewhere unlit has no lamps on, so it is dark.

clue.text: Levels the Spanish put into chosen programme

indicators.note: put into means the Spanish word for the is placed inside the other letters
to programme is to arrange or set up, so the letters of chosen are reorganised

parts.note: el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A TV schedule puts a Spanish show into a selected slot at various levels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'programme' as a verb means arrange, giving ECHONS; the surface reads it as a TV show.
explanation.definitionFit: Echelons are ranks or tiers in an organisation, that is, levels.

clue.text: Easily managed benefit covers islands

indicators.note: covers means the word for benefit wraps round the abbreviation for islands

parts.note: the dole is British slang for state unemployment benefit
CI stands for the Channel Islands

explanation.surface: Welfare payments extend to the islands, making things easy to administer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The dole' is British slang for unemployment benefit; CI is the Channel Islands.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone docile is meek and compliant, readily controlled.

clue.text: Poor Lois arrived outside wearing this!

definitions.text: Poor Lois arrived outside wearing this!

indicators.note: outside means the word for arrived goes round the reworked name

parts.note: came means arrived

indicators.note: poor signals that the letters of Lois are in a bad way and rearranged

explanation.surface: Unlucky Lois turned up out of doors in nothing but her underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' gives ISOL; the whole clue doubles as the definition, picturing Lois out in her underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: A camisole is a light sleeveless top worn as lingerie, hardly street wear.

clue.text: Men condescended to listen and were admitted to church

parts.note: OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers as opposed to officers

indicators.note: to listen means the word for condescended is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: deigned means condescended

explanation.surface: Some men stooped to hear a sermon and were then taken into the church.
explanation.walkthrough: OR (other ranks) is a crossword staple for men; 'and were' joins the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To be ordained is to be formally made a priest or minister, taken into holy orders.

clue.text: Dislike hothead crossed by a mainly tiresome person

indicators.note: crossed by means the head of hot is cut across by the letters around it
mainly means most of the word, so its last letter goes

parts.note: a bore is a tiresome person
the head of the word hot is its first letter, H

explanation.surface: Someone loathes a short-tempered type who keeps running into a dull companion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mainly' trims BORE to BOR; 'crossed by' puts H inside A BOR.
explanation.definitionFit: To abhor something is to detest it, a strong dislike.

clue.text: Abandoned creed and lit out

indicators.note: out signals that the letters are disordered, as in something put out of place

explanation.surface: Someone renounced their faith and walked out of the lit church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges the letters of CREED and LIT together.
explanation.definitionFit: A derelict building or ship has been deserted and left to ruin.

clue.text: If meat's too well-cooked, have fruit

indicators.note: food that is well cooked has been thoroughly worked over, so these letters are mixed up

parts.note: the letters of meat with its s

explanation.surface: A diner advises switching to fruit if the steak has been overdone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well-cooked' rearranges the eight letters of MEATS and TOO; 'If' and 'have' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Tomatoes are botanically fruits, the seed-bearing parts of the plant.

clue.text: Monarch supporting flipping queen, and changing direction

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means the word for monarch sits beneath the other piece
flipping means the word for queen is turned over

parts.note: a queen is a female cat
a king is a monarch

explanation.surface: A ruler backing his wildly fickle consort keeps shifting course.
explanation.walkthrough: In cat breeding a queen is a female cat; 'flipping' gives TAC, and in a down answer 'supporting' means placed underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacking is sailing into the wind by turning the bow through it to change course.

clue.text: One who takes part in sprint run on Sunday

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means the sprint and run pieces are placed after the letter for Sunday

parts.note: to hare is to run very fast, to sprint
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A competitor enters a Sunday sprint race.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'hare' is a British verb for running fast; R is a run in cricket scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharer is someone who has a portion of something along with others.

clue.text: Take over with ease

explanation.definitionFit: To relieve a sentry is to take over their duty; to relieve pain is to lessen it.

clue.text: Bounder, trapped in lawsuits, falls

indicators.note: trapped in means the word for bounder is enclosed by the word for lawsuits

parts.note: cases are lawsuits
a cad is an ungentlemanly bounder

explanation.surface: A rogue caught up in litigation finally comes a cropper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bounder' and 'cad' are old British words for a dishonourable man.
explanation.definitionFit: Cascades are waterfalls, especially small ones in a series.

clue.text: Tree which, placed before man, becomes official

indicators.note: the tree word is the part of the official's title that comes before the word man

parts.note: an alderman is a senior civic official on a council
taken as written

explanation.surface: A riddle about a tree that turns into a council official when you add a man.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards from a British civic dignitary's title, dropping the man; 'becomes' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The alder is a tree of the birch family that grows by water.

clue.text: Of a certain breed of people? That's blackwell opening in the test

definitions.text: Of a certain breed of people

indicators.note: in means the opening letter sits within the word for test

parts.note: a trial is a test

indicators.note: opening picks the first letter of the word blackwell

explanation.surface: A question about breeding answered with a nod to a cricket Test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening' takes B from 'blackwell', and 'in' puts it inside TRIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Tribal describes something belonging to a tribe, a group of people sharing descent.

clue.text: Balloon firstly became floppy

indicators.note: firstly picks out the first letter of the word became

parts.note: limp means floppy and lacking stiffness

explanation.surface: A balloon at a party went soft and saggy.
explanation.definitionFit: A blimp is a non-rigid airship, a large gas-filled balloon.

clue.text: A short note added to end of the recess

parts.note: PS, a postscript, is a short note added to a letter

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of the word the

explanation.surface: A brief message is tacked on at the end of the alcove.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is a semicircular recess at the end of a church.

clue.text: Had nothing to do in paid ledgers

indicators.note: in shows the answer sits inside the words paid ledgers

explanation.surface: An underemployed clerk sat around with the settled accounts books.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who idled lazed about without working.

clue.text: Four in deadlock became poker-faced

indicators.note: in means the numeral for four is placed inside the word for deadlock

parts.note: an impasse is a deadlock
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Four players stuck in a stalemate kept their expressions blank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'became' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Impassive means showing no emotion, the blank expression of a card player hiding their hand.

clue.text: The main point is in when raised

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the letters are read upwards
in means the compass point goes inside the word for when

parts.note: as can mean when
E, east, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A speaker's key argument comes in when he lifts his voice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts E inside AS to make AES, and 'raised' reads that upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The main is a poetic term for the open ocean.

clue.text: Lousy present for the teacher from this individual!

parts.note: rotten means lousy, very bad
an apple is the traditional gift a pupil gives a teacher

explanation.surface: A pupil hands over a bad gift for the teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is a link word; the exclamation mark points to a corrupting person.
explanation.definitionFit: A bad person who corrupts those around them is idiomatically called one bad fruit spoiling the barrel.
